import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Polyhedra with more than seven pairwise adjacent faces

The tetrahedron ($4$ faces, genus $0$) and the Szilassi polyhedron ($7$ hexagonal faces,
genus $1$) are the only known polyhedra in which every face shares an edge with every other
face. Wikipedia asks:

> Is there a non-convex polyhedron without self-intersections with more than seven faces, all of
> which share an edge with each other?

Here a *polyhedron without self-intersections* is a closed surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that is the
union of finitely many planar polygons (its *faces*) with pairwise disjoint relative interiors,
and two faces *share an edge* when their intersection contains a line segment of positive length.

If such a polyhedron has $f$ faces and genus $h$, then a count using the Euler characteristic
gives $h \geq (f-3)(f-4)/12$, with equality when every two faces share exactly one edge and every
vertex has degree $3$; in that case $f \equiv 0, 3, 4, 7 \pmod{12}$. The next candidate after the
Szilassi polyhedron is therefore $f = 12$, $h = 6$, and it is unknown whether it can be realized
without self-intersections.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Szilassi polyhedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Szilassi_polyhedron)
- [Wikipedia, Császár polyhedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cs%C3%A1sz%C3%A1r_polyhedron)
- [GS09] Grünbaum, B., Szilassi, L., *Geometric realizations of special toroidal complexes*,
  Contributions to Discrete Mathematics (2009). [doi:10.11575/cdm.v4i1.61986](https://doi.org/10.11575/cdm.v4i1.61986)
- [AKKLSVW24] Arseneva, E., Kleist, L., Klemz, B., Löffler, M., Schulz, A., Vogtenhuber, B.,
  Wolff, A., *Adjacency graphs of polyhedral surfaces*, Discrete & Computational Geometry (2024).
  [doi:10.1007/s00454-023-00537-6](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-023-00537-6)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace MoreThanSevenFaces

/--
`IsPolygon F` says that `F ⊆ ℝ³` is a (closed, filled, simple) planar polygon: `F` lies in a
plane, `F` is a finite union of nondegenerate triangles, and `F` is homeomorphic to a closed
disk. The last condition rules out polygons with holes and non-simple polygons.
-/
def IsPolygon (F : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  Coplanar ℝ F ∧
    (∃ T : Finset (Affine.Triangle ℝ ℝ³),
      F = ⋃ t ∈ T, convexHull ℝ (Set.range t.points)) ∧
    Nonempty (F ≃ₜ Metric.closedBall (0 : ℝ²) 1)

/--
`IsPolyhedron F` says that the family `F : ι → Set ℝ³` is the family of faces of a polyhedron
without self-intersections in `ℝ³`:
* every `F i` is a planar polygon,
* two distinct faces have disjoint relative interiors (so they can only meet along their
  boundaries),
* the union of the faces is a closed surface, i.e. a compact topological $2$-manifold without
  boundary (compactness is automatic, as a finite union of compact sets).

The faces are allowed to be non-convex polygons. Nothing forces the surface to be the boundary of
a convex solid, so this includes non-convex polyhedra of arbitrary genus.
-/
structure IsPolyhedron {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (F : ι → Set ℝ³) : Prop where
  isPolygon : ∀ i, IsPolygon (F i)
  disjoint_intrinsicInterior :
    Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (intrinsicInterior ℝ (F i)) (intrinsicInterior ℝ (F j))
  isSurface : Nonempty (ChartedSpace ℝ² (⋃ i, F i))

/-- The empty set is not a polygon. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem not_isPolygon_empty : ¬ IsPolygon (∅ : Set ℝ³) := by
  rintro ⟨-, -, ⟨e⟩⟩
  exact (e.symm ⟨0, by simp⟩).2

/-- Polygons are coplanar. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem IsPolygon.coplanar {F : Set ℝ³} (h : IsPolygon F) : Coplanar ℝ F :=
  h.1

/-- Polygons are nonempty. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem IsPolygon.nonempty {F : Set ℝ³} (h : IsPolygon F) : F.Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨-, -, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  exact ⟨_, (e.symm ⟨0, by simp⟩).2⟩

/-- Polygons are compact. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem IsPolygon.isCompact {F : Set ℝ³} (h : IsPolygon F) : IsCompact F := by
  obtain ⟨-, -, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  have : CompactSpace F := e.symm.compactSpace
  exact isCompact_iff_compactSpace.mpr this

/-- The surface of a polyhedron is compact, so it is a closed surface. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem IsPolyhedron.isCompact_iUnion {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] {F : ι → Set ℝ³}
    (h : IsPolyhedron F) : IsCompact (⋃ i, F i) :=
  _root_.isCompact_iUnion fun i => (h.isPolygon i).isCompact

/--
Is there a non-convex polyhedron without self-intersections with more than seven faces, all of
which share an edge with each other?

Formally: is there a polyhedron without self-intersections in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with faces
$F_0, \dots, F_{n-1}$, $n > 7$, which is not the boundary of a convex set, and such that any
two distinct faces $F_i$, $F_j$ share an edge, i.e. $F_i \cap F_j$ contains a line segment of
positive length?

The only known examples of polyhedra in which every two faces share an edge are the tetrahedron
($n = 4$) and the Szilassi polyhedron ($n = 7$). The non-convexity hypothesis is automatic: a
polyhedron with $n > 7$ pairwise adjacent faces has genus at least $2$, so its surface cannot
bound a convex set.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem more_than_seven_faces :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (n : ℕ) (F : Fin n → Set ℝ³), 7 < n ∧ IsPolyhedron F ∧
      (¬ ∃ K : Set ℝ³, Convex ℝ K ∧ (⋃ i, F i) = frontier K) ∧
      ∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∃ a b : ℝ³, a ≠ b ∧ segment ℝ a b ⊆ F i ∩ F j := by
  sorry

end MoreThanSevenFaces
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. One minor remark: the notes say any such polyhedron has f ≡ 0,3,4,7 (mod 12), hence f ≥ 12. That congruence follows from the article's equality h = (f−4)(f−3)/12, which presupposes that every two faces share exactly one edge and every vertex has degree 3; without those extra assumptions only the inequality h ≥ (f−3)(f−4)/12 is available (still forcing genus ≥ 2 for f ≥ 8, so 'non-convex' remains automatic). This does not affect the slot, which is stated with the source's bound `7 < n`.
modeling_decisions: Faces are modelled as sets (planar polygonal disks), not as combinatorial cycles of vertices. 'Without self-intersections' is encoded as: pairwise disjoint relative interiors of faces + the union of faces is a closed topological 2-manifold (`Nonempty (ChartedSpace ℝ² S)`), i.e. an embedded closed polyhedral surface. This is slightly more permissive than Grünbaum-style definitions: it allows T-junctions/straight-angle vertices (a vertex of one face lying in the relative interior of an edge of another) and coplanar edge-adjacent faces. Neither relaxation affects the Euler-characteristic obstruction (genus ≥ (f−3)(f−4)/12), so no cheap examples arise; reviewer should confirm they accept this reading of 'polyhedron'.

'Share an edge' is encoded as: the intersection of the two faces contains a line segment of positive length (`∃ a ≠ b, segment ℝ a b ⊆ F i ∩ F j`), following the decomposition notes; since relative interiors are disjoint, such a segment lies in the boundaries of both faces, i.e. along a common edge.

'Non-convex' is encoded as: the surface ⋃ F i is not the frontier of a convex subset of ℝ³. As the decomposition notes say, this is automatic (n > 7 pairwise adjacent faces force genus ≥ 2, so the surface is not a sphere), but it is included to mirror the source statement; it cannot change the truth value.

Orientability, connectedness and compactness of the surface are not stated separately: an embedded closed surface in ℝ³ is orientable, pairwise adjacency forces connectedness, and a finite union of polygons is compact (proved as API).

Faces are indexed by `Fin n` with `7 < n`; distinctness of faces is automatic because faces are nonempty disks with pairwise disjoint relative interiors. The empty family (n = 0) technically satisfies `IsPolyhedron` but is excluded by `7 < n`.

Faces are allowed to be non-convex simple polygons (as in the Szilassi polyhedron, whose hexagons are non-convex); the disk condition `Nonempty (F ≃ₜ Metric.closedBall (0 : ℝ²) 1)` excludes polygons with holes.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# More Than Seven Faces

Is there an embedded non-convex polyhedron with more than seven faces such that every two
faces share an edge? Here a polyhedron is modeled geometrically as a closed polyhedral surface
in Euclidean three-space, rather than merely as an abstract polytope.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Szilassi polyhedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Szilassi_polyhedron)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry
open Set

namespace MoreThanSevenFaces

/--
A planar polygonal disk in Euclidean three-space. It is represented as a finite union of
nondegenerate triangles lying in an affine plane, and is required to be homeomorphic to a closed
two-dimensional disk. The homeomorphism condition rules out holes and disconnected or singular
unions of triangles.
-/
def IsPlanarPolygonalDisk (s : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ (T : Finset (Fin 3 → ℝ³)) (p : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³),
    Module.finrank ℝ p.direction = 2 ∧
    s ⊆ p ∧
    (∀ t ∈ T, AffineIndependent ℝ t) ∧
    s = ⋃ t ∈ T, convexHull ℝ (Set.range t) ∧
    Nonempty (s ≃ₜ Metric.closedBall (0 : ℝ²) 1)

/--
A finite family of planar polygonal faces forming an embedded closed polyhedral surface in
Euclidean three-space. Local Euclidean neighborhoods say that the union has no boundary or
self-crossing. Distinct faces are required to meet in exactly one nondegenerate closed segment;
thus this segment is a full common edge, rather than merely a common vertex.
-/
def IsEmbeddedClosedPolyhedralSurface {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (face : ι → Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective face ∧
  (∀ i, IsPlanarPolygonalDisk (face i)) ∧
  (∀ x : (⋃ i, face i),
    ∃ U : Set (⋃ i, face i), IsOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ V : Set ℝ², IsOpen V ∧ Nonempty (U ≃ₜ V)) ∧
  ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
    ∃ a b : ℝ³, a ≠ b ∧ face i ∩ face j = segment ℝ a b

/--
Is there a non-convex polyhedron without self-intersections with strictly more than seven faces,
every pair of which shares a full edge? Formally, this asks for an embedded closed polyhedral
surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with planar polygonal-disk faces and more than seven distinct faces,
where the intersection of every two distinct faces is a positive-length segment. For such a
surface with complete face adjacency and more than seven faces, non-convexity is automatic.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52 57]
theorem more_than_seven_faces :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ n : ℕ, 7 < n ∧
        ∃ face : Fin n → Set ℝ³, IsEmbeddedClosedPolyhedralSurface face := by
  sorry

end MoreThanSevenFaces
modeling_decisions: Modeled a polyhedron as a finite family of geometric face subsets of Euclidean three-space whose union is locally homeomorphic to open subsets of ℝ². This makes the carrier an embedded surface without boundary and excludes transverse self-intersections, rather than treating the object as an abstract polytope or immersed surface.

Modeled each planar polygonal face as a finite union of nondegenerate closed triangles in a two-dimensional affine subspace, additionally homeomorphic to a closed two-dimensional disk. This allows nonconvex polygonal faces while excluding holes, disconnected faces, and singular triangle unions.

Required the intersection of every pair of distinct faces to be exactly a closed segment with distinct endpoints. This records a full positive-length common edge and excludes both vertex-only contact and additional unintended pairwise intersections, in line with the polyhedral-surface interpretation underlying the article's Euler-characteristic count.
Indexed faces by Fin n and required the face map to be injective, so n is exactly the number of distinct faces; translated 'more than seven' as the strict inequality 7 < n.

Did not add a separate convexity predicate. For an embedded closed polyhedral surface with complete face adjacency and more than seven faces, the positive-genus Euler-characteristic constraint makes non-convexity automatic. Applying Set.Convex to the surface carrier would instead incorrectly classify even boundaries of ordinary convex polyhedra as non-convex.

/-!
# More than seven faces

This asks whether the tetrahedron and the Szilassi polyhedron can be followed by a
non-self-intersecting polyhedron with more than seven faces and complete face adjacency.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Szilassi polyhedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Szilassi_polyhedron)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace MoreThanSevenFaces

private abbrev Point3 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)
private abbrev Plane2 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)

/-- A subset of three-space is a topological surface without boundary if every point has a
neighborhood homeomorphic to an open subset of the plane. -/
def IsTopologicalSurface (s : Set Point3) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : s, ∃ u : Set s, IsOpen u ∧ x ∈ u ∧
    ∃ v : Set Plane2, IsOpen v ∧ Nonempty (u ≃ₜ v)

/-- `s` is a planar polygonal disk with intrinsic boundary `b`. The triangulation condition makes
it piecewise linear, while the boundary-preserving homeomorphism rules out holes, pinches, and
self-intersecting polygon boundaries. -/
def IsPolygonalFace (s b : Set Point3) : Prop :=
  Coplanar ℝ s ∧
    (∃ triangles : Finset (Affine.Simplex ℝ Point3 2),
      s = ⋃ t ∈ triangles, t.closedInterior) ∧
    ∃ e : Metric.closedBall (0 : Plane2) 1 ≃ₜ s,
      b = {y | ∃ x : Metric.closedBall (0 : Plane2) 1,
        ‖(x : Plane2)‖ = 1 ∧ (e x : Point3) = y} ∧
      ∃ edges : Finset (Point3 × Point3),
        (∀ q ∈ edges, q.1 ≠ q.2) ∧
        b = ⋃ q ∈ edges, segment ℝ q.1 q.2

/-- Geometric data for a finite polyhedral surface in three-space. -/
structure PolyhedronData where
  faces : Finset (Set Point3)
  boundary : Set Point3 → Set Point3

/-- The point set covered by the faces of `P`. -/
def PolyhedronData.surface (P : PolyhedronData) : Set Point3 :=
  ⋃ f ∈ P.faces, f

/-- `P` is a genuine embedded closed polyhedral surface. In particular, every face is a planar
polygonal disk, the whole surface is a compact connected 2-manifold without boundary, and
distinct faces can meet only along their polygon boundaries. -/
def PolyhedronData.IsEmbedded (P : PolyhedronData) : Prop :=
  (∀ f ∈ P.faces, IsPolygonalFace f (P.boundary f)) ∧
    IsCompact P.surface ∧
    IsConnected P.surface ∧
    IsTopologicalSurface P.surface ∧
    (P.faces : Set (Set Point3)).Pairwise fun f g ↦
      f ∩ g ⊆ P.boundary f ∩ P.boundary g

/--
Is there a non-convex polyhedron embedded in $\mathbb{R}^3$ without self-intersections, with
strictly more than seven planar polygonal faces, such that every two distinct faces share a full
positive-length edge? Here the intersection of each pair of faces is required to be exactly that
edge, rather than merely containing a common vertex. With more than seven completely adjacent
faces on a closed polyhedral surface, non-convexity is automatic, so it is not imposed separately.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem more_than_seven_faces :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ P : PolyhedronData, P.IsEmbedded ∧ 7 < P.faces.card ∧
      (P.faces : Set (Set Point3)).Pairwise fun f g ↦
        ∃ a b : Point3, a ≠ b ∧ f ∩ g = segment ℝ a b := by
  sorry

end MoreThanSevenFaces
modeling_decisions: Modeled a genuine geometric polyhedron as a finite family of subsets of Euclidean three-space, rather than as an abstract polytope or an immersed parametrized surface.

Modeled each face as a coplanar disk that is a finite union of nondegenerate closed affine triangles. Its intrinsic circle boundary must be a finite union of nondegenerate line segments. This permits non-convex polygonal faces without permitting holes, pinches, or self-crossing boundaries.

Required the union of the faces to be compact, connected, and locally homeomorphic to open subsets of the Euclidean plane. Since it is literally a subset of Euclidean three-space, this expresses an embedded closed surface without boundary; the pairwise boundary-intersection condition additionally rules out crossings through face interiors.

Interpreted 'all of which share an edge with each other' pairwise: every two distinct faces have intersection exactly a positive-length segment. Exact intersection captures a full common edge and excludes mere vertex contact or additional improper intersections.

Used the strict bound `7 < P.faces.card`. Did not separately impose non-convexity: for a closed polyhedral surface with more than seven completely pairwise-adjacent faces, the Euler-characteristic relation cited by the background forces positive genus, so convexity is impossible.

coplanar, the faces around each vertex form a single cycle, and the faces are connected.

order: `vertex j` is joined by an edge to `vertex (finRotate numVertices j)`, the next vertex in the
cycle. -/

  /-- The number of vertices. -/
  numVertices : ℕ
  /-- The vertices, in cyclic order. -/

def vertexSet : Set ℝ³ := Set.range P.vertex

/-- The plane of a polygon: the affine span of its vertices. -/

  triangles.Finite ∧
    (∀ triangle ∈ triangles,
      triangle.Finite ∧ triangle.ncard = 3 ∧
        AffineIndependent ℝ ((↑) : triangle → ℝ³)) ∧
    ∀ triangle₁ ∈ triangles, ∀ triangle₂ ∈ triangles,
      convexHull ℝ triangle₁ ∩ convexHull ℝ triangle₂ =

realization lies in an affine plane and is homeomorphic to a closed disk.

  IsGeometricTriangleComplex triangles ∧

    Nonempty

private abbrev Point3 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

/-- A subset of three-space is locally a topological surface without boundary if every point has
an open neighborhood homeomorphic to an open subset of the Euclidean plane. -/
def IsSurfaceWithoutBoundary (s : Set Point3) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : s, ∃ u : Set s, x ∈ u ∧ IsOpen u ∧
    ∃ v : Set ℝ², IsOpen v ∧ Nonempty (u ≃ₜ v)

/-- A planar polygonal disk in three-space. Its polygonality is expressed by a finite
triangulation, and its boundary is recorded as a finite union of nondegenerate line segments. -/
structure PolygonalFace where
  carrier : Set Point3
  plane : AffineSubspace ℝ Point3
  plane_dim : Module.finrank ℝ plane.direction = 2
  triangles : Finset (Fin 3 → Point3)
  triangles_in_plane : ∀ t ∈ triangles, Set.range t ⊆ plane
  carrier_eq_triangles :
    carrier = ⋃ t ∈ (triangles : Set (Fin 3 → Point3)), convexHull ℝ (Set.range t)
  isDisk : Nonempty (Metric.closedBall (0 : ℝ²) 1 ≃ₜ carrier)
  edges : Finset (Point3 × Point3)
  edge_nondegenerate : ∀ e ∈ edges, e.1 ≠ e.2
  boundary_eq_edges :
    Subtype.val '' frontier (Subtype.val ⁻¹' carrier : Set plane) =
      ⋃ e ∈ (edges : Set (Point3 × Point3)), segment ℝ e.1 e.2

/-- Faces `i` and `j` meet along the specified full boundary edge `e` of face `i`. The same
geometric segment must be a boundary edge of face `j`, and the two carriers have no further
intersection. -/
def FacesMeetAlong {n : ℕ} (face : Fin n → PolygonalFace) (i j : Fin n)
    (e : Point3 × Point3) : Prop :=
  e ∈ (face i).edges ∧ ∃ e' ∈ (face j).edges,
    segment ℝ e.1 e.2 = segment ℝ e'.1 e'.2 ∧
      (face i).carrier ∩ (face j).carrier = segment ℝ e.1 e.2

/-- A genuine embedded closed polyhedral surface in three-space. Distinct polygonal faces have
 distinct carriers and may intersect only along a full boundary edge. Every boundary edge is
 incident to exactly one other face, and the geometric union is compact, connected, and locally
 a surface without boundary. -/
structure EmbeddedPolyhedralSurface (n : ℕ) where
  face : Fin n → PolygonalFace
  face_injective : Function.Injective (fun i ↦ (face i).carrier)
  face_intersections : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
    Disjoint (face i).carrier (face j).carrier ∨ ∃ e, FacesMeetAlong face i j e
  exactly_two_faces_per_edge : ∀ i e, e ∈ (face i).edges →
    ∃! j, j ≠ i ∧ FacesMeetAlong face i j e
  compact : IsCompact (⋃ i, (face i).carrier)
  connected : IsConnected (⋃ i, (face i).carrier)
  locally_surface : IsSurfaceWithoutBoundary (⋃ i, (face i).carrier)

/-- Two distinct faces of a polyhedral surface share a full positive-length edge. -/
def ShareEdge {n : ℕ} (P : EmbeddedPolyhedralSurface n) (i j : Fin n) : Prop :=
  ∃ e, FacesMeetAlong P.face i j e

Is there a non-self-intersecting non-convex polyhedron with strictly more than seven planar
polygonal faces such that every pair of distinct faces shares a full common edge? Here a
polyhedron is modeled as a compact connected embedded closed polyhedral surface in
$\mathbb{R}^3$. For more than seven mutually adjacent faces such a surface necessarily has
positive genus, so non-convexity is automatic.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem more_than_seven_faces :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, 7 < n ∧ ∃ P : EmbeddedPolyhedralSurface n,
      ∀ i j : Fin n, i ≠ j → ShareEdge P i j := by
  sorry

end MoreThanSevenFaces

/-!
# More than seven faces

The tetrahedron and the Szilassi polyhedron (a toroidal polyhedron with seven hexagonal
faces) are the only known polyhedra in which each face shares an edge with each other face.
Wikipedia asks:

> Is there a non-convex polyhedron without self-intersections with more than seven faces,
> all of which share an edge with each other?

## Formalisation

A *polyhedron without self-intersections* is modelled by its surface `S ⊆ ℝ³`:
a connected finite union of non-degenerate triangles which is a topological surface
without boundary (every point has a neighbourhood in `S` homeomorphic to an open subset of
$\mathbb{R}^2$). The surface condition is exactly the absence of self-intersections: two faces
crossing each other, or touching at an interior point, destroy the manifold property.
Being a finite union of compact triangles, `S` is compact, hence a closed surface, and the
Euler-characteristic argument of the Wikipedia article applies to it.

The *faces* of `S` are recovered from `S` itself: a point of `S` is *flat* if some
neighbourhood of it in `S` lies in a plane, and the faces are the closures of the connected
components of the set of flat points. Every face is required to be a simple planar polygon,
i.e. homeomorphic to a closed disc. With this convention adjacent coplanar polygons are merged
into a single face (a genuine polyhedron has no coplanar adjacent faces), so the face count
cannot be inflated by subdividing a face.

Two faces *share an edge* if their intersection contains a line segment of positive length
(so sharing a single vertex does not count).

*References:*
 - [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
 - [Wikipedia, Szilassi polyhedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Szilassi_polyhedron)
 - [Grünbaum, Szilassi, *Geometric realizations of special toroidal complexes*](https://doi.org/10.11575/cdm.v4i1.61986)
-/

open Topology
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace MoreThanSevenFaces

/-- The *flat points* of a set `S ⊆ ℝ³`: the points of `S` having a neighbourhood in `S`
contained in a plane. For a polyhedral surface these are the points lying in the relative
interior of a face. -/
def flatPoints (S : Set ℝ³) : Set ℝ³ :=
  {x ∈ S | ∃ U ∈ 𝓝 x, Coplanar ℝ (S ∩ U)}

/-- The *faces* of a set `S ⊆ ℝ³`: the closures of the connected components of the set of
flat points of `S`. -/
def faces (S : Set ℝ³) : Set (Set ℝ³) :=
  {F | ∃ x ∈ flatPoints S, F = closure (connectedComponentIn (flatPoints S) x)}

/-- Two faces `F` and `G` *share an edge* if their intersection contains a line segment of
positive length. Faces meeting only in a vertex do not share an edge. -/
def ShareEdge (F G : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b : ℝ³, a ≠ b ∧ segment ℝ a b ⊆ F ∩ G

/-- `S ⊆ ℝ³` is the surface of a *polyhedron without self-intersections*:
* `S` is a finite union of non-degenerate triangles (so it is compact and made of finitely
  many planar polygons);
* `S` is connected;
* `S` is a topological surface without boundary, i.e. a closed embedded surface; this is the
  "no self-intersections" requirement;
* every face of `S` (see `MoreThanSevenFaces.faces`) is a simple planar polygon, i.e. is
  homeomorphic to a closed disc. -/
structure IsPolyhedralSurface (S : Set ℝ³) : Prop where
  exists_triangles : ∃ T : Finset (Fin 3 → ℝ³),
    (∀ t ∈ T, AffineIndependent ℝ t) ∧ S = ⋃ t ∈ T, convexHull ℝ (Set.range t)
  isConnected : IsConnected S
  chartedSpace : Nonempty (ChartedSpace ℝ² S)
  faces_disc : ∀ F ∈ faces S, Nonempty (F ≃ₜ Metric.closedBall (0 : ℝ²) 1)

@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem ShareEdge.symm {F G : Set ℝ³} (h : ShareEdge F G) : ShareEdge G F := by
  obtain ⟨a, b, hab, h⟩ := h
  exact ⟨a, b, hab, h.trans (Set.inter_comm F G).subset⟩

@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem IsPolyhedralSurface.isCompact {S : Set ℝ³} (hS : IsPolyhedralSurface S) :
    IsCompact S := by
  obtain ⟨T, -, rfl⟩ := hS.exists_triangles
  exact T.finite_toSet.isCompact_biUnion fun t _ ↦ (Set.finite_range t).isCompact_convexHull

@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem IsPolyhedralSurface.subset_of_mem_faces {S F : Set ℝ³} (hS : IsPolyhedralSurface S)
    (hF : F ∈ faces S) : F ⊆ S := by
  obtain ⟨x, -, rfl⟩ := hF
  exact closure_minimal ((connectedComponentIn_subset _ _).trans (Set.sep_subset _ _))
    hS.isCompact.isClosed

/--
Is there a non-convex polyhedron without self-intersections with more than seven faces,
all of which share an edge with each other?

Here a polyhedron without self-intersections is given by its surface `S ⊆ ℝ³`, a closed
embedded polyhedral surface with simple planar polygonal faces (`IsPolyhedralSurface`);
it is non-convex when `S` is not the boundary of a convex set; its faces are the maximal
planar pieces of `S` (`faces S`); and two faces share an edge when their intersection
contains a segment of positive length (`ShareEdge`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem more_than_seven_faces :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S : Set ℝ³, IsPolyhedralSurface S ∧
      (¬ ∃ K : Set ℝ³, Convex ℝ K ∧ frontier K = S) ∧
      7 < (faces S).encard ∧
      (faces S).Pairwise ShareEdge := by
  sorry

end MoreThanSevenFaces

genus $1$) are the only known polyhedra in which every face shares an edge with every other
face. If a polyhedron with $f$ faces and $h$ holes has this property, then Euler's formula
gives $h \geq (f-4)(f-3)/12$, with equality when each vertex has degree $3$ and each pair of

seven faces, all of which share an edge with each other?*

(a compact topological $2$-manifold without boundary). The last condition is what "without
self-intersections" means: the surface is embedded in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Two faces *share an edge*
if their intersection contains a line segment of positive length.

- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

namespace MoreThanSevenFaces

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

/--
A set $F \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is a *polygon* (a simple, not necessarily convex, planar polygon
together with its interior) if it lies in a plane, is homeomorphic to a closed disk, and its
boundary relative to that plane is a finite union of line segments.
-/
def IsPolygon (F : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  Coplanar ℝ F ∧
  Nonempty (F ≃ₜ Metric.closedBall (0 : ℝ²) 1) ∧
  ∃ E : Finset (ℝ³ × ℝ³), intrinsicFrontier ℝ F = ⋃ e ∈ E, segment ℝ e.1 e.2

/-- Two faces *share an edge* if their intersection contains a line segment of positive
length (and not merely a vertex). -/
def SharesEdge (F G : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b : ℝ³, a ≠ b ∧ segment ℝ a b ⊆ F ∩ G

/--
A finite set `faces` of subsets of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a *polyhedron without self-intersections*
if
- every face is a planar simple polygon (`IsPolygon`);
- two distinct faces meet only along their boundaries;
- two faces sharing an edge are not coplanar (so faces are genuine faces, not pieces of a
  larger planar face);
- the union of the faces is connected;
- the union of the faces is a topological $2$-manifold without boundary (it is automatically
  compact). Together with the previous conditions this says that the surface is embedded in
  $\mathbb{R}^3$: faces meet only along common edges and vertices, every edge lies in exactly
  two faces, and the faces around each vertex form a single cycle.
-/
structure IsPolyhedron (faces : Finset (Set ℝ³)) : Prop where
  isPolygon : ∀ F ∈ faces, IsPolygon F
  inter_subset_frontier : ∀ F ∈ faces, ∀ G ∈ faces, F ≠ G →
    F ∩ G ⊆ intrinsicFrontier ℝ F ∩ intrinsicFrontier ℝ G
  not_coplanar : ∀ F ∈ faces, ∀ G ∈ faces, F ≠ G → SharesEdge F G →
    ¬ Coplanar ℝ (F ∪ G)
  isConnected : IsConnected (⋃₀ (faces : Set (Set ℝ³)))
  chartedSpace : Nonempty (ChartedSpace ℝ² (⋃₀ (faces : Set (Set ℝ³))))

/-- A polyhedron is *convex* if its surface is the boundary of a convex set. -/

  obtain ⟨a, b, hab, h⟩ := h
  exact ⟨a, b, hab, Set.inter_comm F G ▸ h⟩

/-- Two faces sharing an edge have nonempty intersection. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem SharesEdge.nonempty_inter {F G : Set ℝ³} (h : SharesEdge F G) : (F ∩ G).Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨a, b, -, h⟩ := h
  exact ⟨a, h (left_mem_segment ℝ a b)⟩

/-- Two faces whose intersection has at most one point do not share an edge. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem not_sharesEdge_of_subsingleton {F G : Set ℝ³} (h : (F ∩ G).Subsingleton) :
    ¬ SharesEdge F G := by
  rintro ⟨a, b, hab, hs⟩
  exact hab (h (hs (left_mem_segment ℝ a b)) (hs (right_mem_segment ℝ a b)))

/-- A polygon is nonempty. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem IsPolygon.nonempty {F : Set ℝ³} (h : IsPolygon F) : F.Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨-, ⟨e⟩, -⟩ := h
  exact ⟨e.symm ⟨0, Metric.mem_closedBall_self zero_le_one⟩, Subtype.coe_prop _⟩

/-- The empty set is not a polygon. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem not_isPolygon_empty : ¬ IsPolygon (∅ : Set ℝ³) := fun h ↦ by
  simpa using h.nonempty

/--
Is there a non-convex polyhedron without self-intersections with more than seven faces, all of
which share an edge with each other?

The only known polyhedra all of whose faces are pairwise adjacent are the tetrahedron and the
Szilassi polyhedron. (Non-convexity is automatic for more than seven faces, since such a
polyhedron must have genus at least $6$; it is included to match the statement.)
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem more_than_seven_faces :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ faces : Finset (Set ℝ³), 7 < faces.card ∧ IsPolyhedron faces ∧
      ¬ IsConvexPolyhedron faces ∧
      ∀ F ∈ faces, ∀ G ∈ faces, F ≠ G → SharesEdge F G := by
  sorry

end MoreThanSevenFaces
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single slot matches the statement; the note that non-convexity is automatic is correct, and I nonetheless kept the hypothesis literally (it does not alter the statement's truth value).
modeling_decisions: Polyhedron is modelled set-theoretically: a `Finset (Set ℝ³)` of faces (so the face count is `faces.card`, and injectivity is automatic), rather than a combinatorial map plus vertex coordinates. This sidesteps questions about which points count as vertices (e.g. straight angles / T-junction points) since only the point sets matter.

`IsPolygon F` := `Coplanar ℝ F ∧ Nonempty (F ≃ₜ closedBall (0:ℝ²) 1) ∧ ∃ E : Finset (ℝ³ × ℝ³), intrinsicFrontier ℝ F = ⋃ e ∈ E, segment ℝ e.1 e.2`. A planar set homeomorphic to a closed disk whose relative boundary is a finite union of segments is exactly a (closed) simple polygon region; convexity of faces is deliberately NOT required (the Szilassi polyhedron has non-convex hexagonal faces). Faces with holes are excluded, matching the standard requirement that faces are simple polygons.

'Without self-intersections' is modelled as: (a) distinct faces intersect only inside both relative boundaries (`F ∩ G ⊆ intrinsicFrontier ℝ F ∩ intrinsicFrontier ℝ G`), and (b) the union of the faces is a topological 2-manifold without boundary, expressed as `Nonempty (ChartedSpace ℝ² ↥(⋃₀ ↑faces))` (same convention as `Wikipedia/BingBorsuk.lean`). Together these force every boundary point of a face to be matched by exactly one other face, exclude pinched vertices, triple edges, and touching of far parts of the surface, i.e. the surface is embedded. Compactness is automatic (finite union of disks).

Edge-adjacent faces are required to be non-coplanar (`SharesEdge F G → ¬ Coplanar ℝ (F ∪ G)`). This is not literally in the Wikipedia sentence but is part of what 'face of a polyhedron' means (without it the face count is ill-defined: any face could be subdivided, and planar regions with holes could be simulated by coplanar pieces). Coplanar faces that are disjoint or meet only at a point remain allowed, as usual for non-convex polyhedra. A reviewer should confirm this matches the intended (Szilassi/Grünbaum) notion.
Connectedness of the surface is included in `IsPolyhedron` (a polyhedron is connected); it is redundant given pairwise adjacency but harmless.

'Share an edge' is `SharesEdge F G := ∃ a b, a ≠ b ∧ segment ℝ a b ⊆ F ∩ G` (positive-length common segment, not merely a common vertex), following the decomposition note. Under the manifold + proper-intersection conditions any such segment is contained in a genuine edge of the polyhedron shared by exactly these two faces. T-junctions (a face with a straight angle at a vertex of the polyhedron) are allowed, as they are geometrically legitimate polyhedra.

'Non-convex' is included literally as `¬ IsConvexPolyhedron faces` where `IsConvexPolyhedron faces := ∃ K, Convex ℝ K ∧ frontier K = ⋃₀ ↑faces`. As the decomposition note observes, it is mathematically automatic for more than seven faces (genus ≥ 6), so including it does not change the statement's truth; it is kept to match the text.
Number of faces: strict inequality `7 < faces.card`, matching 'more than seven'. The f = 12, h = 6 remark from the article is not stated separately, following the decomposition table.
